newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Mar 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Mar 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which has confronted Australia with the most serious foreign policy crisis since the 1987 Fiji coup, Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok, the commander of the Papua New Guinea Defence Force who yesterday gave Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan and senior Government ministers 48 hours to resign over plans to use mercenaries on Bougainville or face a possible takeover, was sacked last night. Page 1.

In response to the national crisis affecting legal aid programs in the wake of the Commonwealth's proposal to renegotiate legal aid agreements with the States and Territories, the Victorian Bar Council announced yesterday Victorian barristers who accept ofers of retainers from the State's legal aid authority - Victorian Legal Aid - will be removed from the Bar roll. Page 1.

Under a plan approved by Federal Cabinet yesterday expected to attract strong criticism from key players in the A$4 billion meat industry, Australia's three major industry statutory bodies - the Australian Meat and Livestock Corporation, the Meat ResearchCorporation and the Meat Industry Council - will be abolished. Page 3.

A confidential report by the Centre for International Economics, commissioned by State forestry ministers, recommends the privatisation of Australia's A$4 billion, 760,000 hectares of publicly-owned forest plantations, but warned international investors may ignore opportunities for value-added processing . Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A spokesman for Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday the Government is following the situation in Papua New Guinea very closely and with great concern after Papua New Guinea Defence Force commander Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok gave Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan 48 hours to resign over his Government's plans to send mercenaries to Bougainville. Police Commissioner Bob Nenta has backed the Chan Government against the army revolt, causing a split in the country's security forces. Page 1.

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco has been suspended until May 27, 2000 after the International Amateur Athletic Federation overturned a decision by Athletics Australia to allow Capobianco to compete due to flaws in the chain of custody of a urine sampl taken from the Perth sprinter at a grand prix meeting in Holland on May 27 last year. Page 1.

After touring 11 of Australia's universities, Rod West, the chairman of the Federal Government's higher education review, said yesterday there was widespread duplication of courses. He raised the prospect of resurrecting the Commonwealth Tertiary Educatin Commission, a regulatory body axed 10 years ago because it was too powerful and a barrier to change. Page 3.

As fears grow for the safety of 27-year-old solicitor Ciara Glennon, missing since Friday night after attending a pub in the Perth suburb of Claremont, Detective Superintendent Paul Ferguson yesterday revealed police believe a person in a position of trus such as a police officer, security guard or taxi driver may be behind what is feared to be a serial killing case. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a surprise to the Australian Government, Papua New Guinea fell into political turmoil yesterday when the country's army commander, Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok, called on Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to resign over the planned use of foreign mercnaries on Bougainville. His call resulted in his sacking by the PNG Cabinet last night. Page 1.

In the first such arrangement for Australia's oldest university, Sydney University has guaranteed 50 students places in its commerce degree to the Universal Education Centre, a private college run by Dr Anna Ciccarelli, a former student and friend of Sydny University Deputy Vice-Chancellor Professor Ken Ellis, who set up the controversial program. Page 1.

Under a proposal put before the Industrial Relations Commission yesterday, the Howard Government will have to renegotiate its legislation on Medicare access for junior doctors after New South Wales doctors voted last night to restart work at 8am tomorrow fter their week-long strike. Page 3.

A terminally ill woman suffering from carcinoid syndrome, a rare cancer of the gut, has written to all senators appealing to allow her to die using the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia legislation. The woman says the impending vote on Liberal MP evin Andrew's Bill, that could overturn the Territory's Rights of the Terminally Ill Act puts her in an "impossible position" as she does not want to end her life prematurely. Page 3.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday called for a peaceful solution to the Bougainville crisis in accordance with Papua New Guinea's Constitution. His comments come as tension intensifies between Papua New Guinea police and military, with the country's Prme Minister Sir Julius Chan last night rejecting an ultimatum by armed forces chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok to resign over the Government's hiring of mercenaries on Bougainville. Page 1.

The International Amateur Athletic Federation's arbitration panel in Monte Carlo has overturned a decision by Athletics Australia to allow Australian Olympic sprinter Dean Capobianco to compete, suspending him for three years after he was found guilty of aking steroids. Page 1.

For the first time, Melbourne's Anzac Day march chief marshal Brigadier Keith Rossi has written to war veterans to inform them their children and grandchildren are not welcome in the parade as the presence of children breaches the aim of the event - to renite veterans in their wartime units and march to the Shrine of Remembrance to honour dead comrades. Page 1.

After years of campaigning for a ban on battery hen cages, RSPCA president Hugh Wirth yesterday announced that as part of an effort to spark a community-led revolution against the cages, the RSPCA had joined the Farm Pride company to guarantee that barn-lid eggs sold under the brand name Mrs McKechie's would be produced humanely. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
